title: Microsoft adds GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra to Copilot, with wider Astra access tied to Frontier
summary: Microsoft adds GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra to Copilot with wider access
detailed: Microsoft integrated OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra models into its Copilot work products for document editing, spreadsheets, and business tasks.
Sol has a broader worldwide reach across Copilot Chat, Cowork, Studio, and Office apps, while Astra's access in Office apps is tied to the Frontier program.
Involved companies include Microsoft and OpenAI, with administrative controls managed through the Microsoft 365 admin centre.
The integration uses the Work IQ layer to supply context from workplace data while respecting existing permissions, improving task accuracy and usefulness for enterprise users.
sentences: Microsoft has begun bringing OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol alongside the GPT-6.2 Astra model into its Copilot work products, extending the models to document editing, spreadsheets and other business tasks.
The company announced the rollout on 20 November, but the two options will not appear in exactly the same places for every eligible user.
Sol has the broader initial reach across Microsoft's productivity apps.
Astra is also coming to Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio, while access through Copilot Chat, Word, Excel and PowerPoint is being offered to Frontier users.
Microsoft says Sol is being introduced worldwide across Copilot Chat, Cowork and Studio, alongside Copilot within Word, PowerPoint and Excel.
Its announcement describes availability for eligible users rather than a release open to everyone with one of those applications.
Astra follows a narrower route in the familiar Office apps.
Microsoft's Frontier programme provides access there and in Chat, in addition to the model's rollout in Cowork and Studio.
That distinction matters because the announcement is about several Copilot products, not one identical upgrade across the entire range.
The company also cautions that regions and organisations may receive access differently.
A worldwide rollout therefore does not establish that every account in India, or every employee within a business, already has both choices.
Microsoft has not given a single completion date in its public announcement.
The integration also uses Microsoft's Work IQ layer to supply context from workplace information.
Microsoft identifies files, meeting material, chats and business data as sources that can help the models respond to a task.
According to the company, this process respects permissions already assigned to each person.
It is not presented as permission for an employee to retrieve colleagues' restricted material simply by choosing a different model.
Microsoft argues that combining a model with relevant company information improves the usefulness and accuracy of its answers.
Those are the company's claims about the integration, rather than results from an independent comparison of the new Copilot options.
OpenAI describes Astra as its option for difficult professional projects and Sol as a more efficient choice for everyday work.
Its launch material points to documents, spreadsheets, presentations and coding among the areas where it says the models have improved.
Organisations retain administrative control over availability through the Microsoft 365 admin centre, Microsoft says.
Its public post does not set out one universal price for the new options.
Microsoft is widening the places where its customers can use OpenAI's latest models, with Sol reaching more work apps and Astra access varying by product and Frontier eligibility.
The stated worldwide rollout still comes with regional and organisational limits, so the announcement should not be read as confirmation that both models are already available to every Copilot user.
